root_motivation: Three SKILL.md bugs shipped to production from /self-review this week because no install-time validation exists: a malformed YAML key, an undocumented `Skill(...)` invocation, and a stale binary version reference. A standalone `skill validate` CLI catches structural mistakes before invocation and gives CI, editor save hooks, and the Claude Code loader a single source-of-truth schema. Phase 0 (this slice) is the parser + validator + schema only; later phases (deps, test, scaffold, graph) compose on top.
user_persona: jsy and future Claude sessions on this laptop, invoking `skill validate <name|path>` from a shell, a pre-commit hook, or the SessionStart hook list. Output consumed by humans reading errors and by tooling parsing the structured JSON `--format json` output. ~14 installed skills today; growth expected as plugins proliferate.

acceptance_criteria.description: CLI binary `skill` accepts the positional subcommand `validate` followed by a path or skill-name argument. `skill validate <path-to-skill-md>` reads the file, parses its YAML frontmatter, and emits a structured verdict.
A SKILL.md with no `manifest:` block validates successfully (backwards compatibility). Output: `verdict: pass`, `manifest_present: false`, `warnings: []`. Exit code 0.

A SKILL.md with a well-formed `manifest:` block (version, requires.binaries, requires.skills, exports, tests — each optional) validates successfully. Output: `verdict: pass`, `manifest_present: true`, with the parsed manifest echoed in the JSON output. Exit code 0.

Validates the `manifest.version` field as semver (`^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[A-Za-z0-9.-]+)?$`). Non-semver versions emit `verdict: fail` with error `id: invalid_semver`, `path: manifest.version`, and the offending value. Exit code 1.

Validates that each entry in `manifest.requires.binaries` has a required `name` field and an optional `version` field (semver-range constraint, e.g. `>=0.3.0`, `>=1.0.0,<2.0.0`). Missing `name` → `verdict: fail`, error `id: missing_required_field`, `path: manifest.requires.binaries[N].name`.

Rejects unknown top-level manifest keys (`additionalProperties: false`). Output: `verdict: fail`, error `id: unknown_field`, `path: manifest.<unknown_key>`. Known top-level keys: `version`, `requires`, `exports`, `inputs`, `tests`.
Malformed YAML frontmatter (truncated, unclosed quote, tab indentation) → `verdict: fail`, error `id: yaml_parse_error` with the underlying parser message. Exit code 1.

Invocation errors (path does not exist, file unreadable, unknown subcommand) → exit code 2. Stdout is empty; stderr contains a single human-readable diagnostic line. JSON mode emits `{verdict: "error", error: {...}}` to stdout in this case.
`skill validate <skill-name>` (no slash, no `.md` extension) resolves to `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. If that file doesn't exist, falls back to error path `unknown_skill` with exit code 2.

`--format json` (default `text`) emits a single JSON object to stdout matching the schema `skill_manifest.verdict.v1` (verdict, manifest_present, manifest, warnings, errors). Deterministic key ordering; same input always produces byte-identical output.

scope: Rust 2024 CLI crate `skill-manifest` producing a `skill` binary.
YAML frontmatter parsing (--- fenced) of SKILL.md files.
JSON-schema-style validation of the optional `manifest:` block (semver, required fields, additionalProperties: false).
Two output formats: human-readable text (default) and stable structured JSON (--format json).
Exit code mapping: 0 = valid, 1 = validation failures, 2 = invocation errors.
Resolution of bare skill names to ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md.
Unit + acceptance tests using fixture SKILL.md files committed under tests/fixtures/.
non_goals: Not the Claude Code skill loader. This is an out-of-process validator; the loader integration is a separate piece of work.
Not skill installation or dependency resolution. `skill deps` is Phase 1, out of this slice.
Not skill testing. `skill test` is Phase 2, out of this slice.
Not skill scaffolding. `skill scaffold` is Phase 3, out of this slice.
Not sandbox enforcement. The manifest is documentation + lint, not a runtime restriction.
Not auto-installing missing binaries listed in requires.binaries.
Not a generic YAML linter — only SKILL.md frontmatter shapes are recognized.

five_whys_trace.a: Three SKILL.md bugs shipped to production from /self-review this week because no install-time validation exists. The manifest schema catches structural mistakes before invocation.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a separate CLI instead of inline validation in the Claude Code loader?
five_whys_trace.a: Out-of-process validation runs in CI, in editor save hooks, on git pre-commit — places the loader doesn't reach. The loader can call this CLI; CI/editor can call it independently.
Bootstrap. Get the schema right and ship; later phases (deps, test, scaffold) build on the parser. If the schema needs to change, doing it later breaks downstream consumers.

five_whys_trace.q: Why backwards-compatible (no manifest block = old behavior)?
five_whys_trace.a: 14+ existing skills don't have manifests yet. A breaking change blocks adoption; opt-in lets manifests proliferate gradually.

five_whys_trace.q: Why now and not after agentic-memory v0.2?
five_whys_trace.a: The pain is current — three SKILL.md bugs already shipped this week. The v0.2 dependency isn't on the critical path; skill-manifest can ship independently and unblock v0.2's quality work.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should the validator load the SessionStart hook to run automatically, or just be invokable?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Just invokable in this slice. Loader integration is Phase 1; running it at SessionStart for every installed skill is a separate concern that depends on the validator being stable first.

ambiguities_resolved.question: How strict is unknown-key handling — warning or error?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Error. additionalProperties:false at the manifest top level. Skill authors who want a custom field can extend the schema explicitly via a future amendment.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Is the input-schema validation (JSON Schema draft-07) in scope?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Out of this slice. The `inputs:` block is parsed and stored but not used to validate actual skill invocations — that's Phase 1 loader work. Validator only checks that `inputs:` is a well-formed JSON-schema-shaped object.
